restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM, collision-frontier-v5, C = 2644; total work over all processors. Family m(g,t) = P || BE128(g XOR R0) || BE24(t) (55 bytes, one padded block) with coins P (288 bits) and R0 (128 bits) drawn once per run; N = 7*2^24*ceil(2^104/7) >= 2^128 distinct messages, groups g = 7k+l. Rounds 0..12 per group batch; key needs rounds 13..34 and round 35's E half (round 36 skipped).

Counted straight-line 7-lane 36-bit-guard SWAR batch (H2): 1406 operations per 7 messages (rounds 1092, schedule 193, key 62, table 55, loop 4), 44 persistent registers plus at most 20 live values. Group setup 2^20 per 7*2^24 messages; cold path regenerates both messages from their 136-bit indices and recompresses: 2 compressions + 512 operations per call, at most V+1 calls.

144-bit key from digest words d,c,h,g,f probes a never-initialised 2^144-word table holding a 120-bit TAG and the index; the worst-case ledger charges the cap V, not an expectation. Success 0.39 is conditional on H1 (99% of the random-function collision exponent) and H2. Memory 2^150 bytes is address span, reported only. No witness or executed search is asserted.

heuristics.statement: For the N = 7*2^24*ceil(2^104/7) reduced r37 digests of the deterministic family m(g,t) in the fixed processing order, with probability over the run's uniform coins P and R0, assume Pr[F1] <= exp(-0.99*N(N-1)/2^257), Pr[F2] <= N^3/(3*2^400), E[Y1] <= N^2/2^144 and Var[Y1] <= N^2/2^144, where F1 is the absence of an equal-digest pair, F2 an intervening overwrite of a colliding pair in the uninitialised table, and Y1 the number of different-digest pairs with equal 144-bit keys. These are 99% of the random-function F1 exponent and twice the random-function F2 and Y1 values.
heuristics.scope: Full-scale collision existence, table retention and candidate-count moments for this family, in which within a run about 104 group bits and 24 counter bits vary. Garbage and TAG terms are bounded without it. It does not establish implementation equivalence (H2).
heuristics.extrapolation: Two organizer experiments run a scaled copy of the same algorithm (index map, round-skip key bits, uninitialised table with garbage, TAG, regeneration, cap) on this family and reduced hash with a 16-bit digest. Pre-registered ideal-model predictions: h1-success 0.6163 per trial, 99.9% decision interval [131, 184] of 256; h1-overwrite missed collisions 0.1538, interval [21, 60]. Scaled counts cannot certify the 256-bit regime or the 1% exponent tolerance.
heuristics.limitations: Unproved full-scale event and moment bounds for a structured family; 16-bit scaled trials resolve only roughly 10-20% rate shifts.

heuristics.statement: The counted 7-lane SWAR batch in experiments/replay.py computes, for every input of the family, the seven reference 144-bit keys of the scalar r37 core, at exactly 1406 operations per batch with 44 persistent registers and at most 20 other live values.
heuristics.scope: Implementation equivalence and exact operation count of the per-message batch.
heuristics.extrapolation: The batch is straight-line with a data-independent operation sequence; every addition carries a static lane bound below 2^36 and the mask identities are exact; h1-success trial 0 re-runs it on 4 organizer-seeded group batches of the family and aborts the experiment on any lane or count mismatch. Finite checks extrapolate to all inputs through the static argument.
heuristics.limitations: The organizer trusts only the returned pairs; the self-check numbers are untrusted observations, and the abort-on-mismatch is visible only in the source.
